Lemma
[Properties of Derivations]

1. ch3:3.1Let $a\in \mathbb {R}^n$, $w\in T_a\mathbb {R}^n$, and $f,g\in C^\infty (\mathbb {R}^n)$. Then:

  1. if $f$ is constant, then $w(f)=0$;

  2. if $f(a)=g(a)=0$, then $w(fg)=0$.

Proof

\sketch For the constant function $1$, the product rule gives $w(1)=w(1\cdot 1)=2w(1)$, hence $w(1)=0$; linearity handles every constant. If $f(a)=g(a)=0$, (3.3) gives $w(fg)=0$ directly.

□
